Harbour freight

Late deliveries fell by a third once the night shift moved to the dock.

The third quarter review covers 41,280 consignments across four routes. Most of the gain came from one scheduling change, and one route still needs attention.

What changed

Until July the night shift loaded trailers in the yard, a ten minute walk from the sorting floor. Moving the shift to the covered dock removed that walk and let two loaders share one scanner station.

The effect showed within two weeks. Trailers on the northern and coastal routes left on time on 96 of 100 nights, against 81 of 100 in the second quarter.

Three things to do next

Fix the valley route handover

Drivers on the valley route still wait for paperwork at the second depot. A shared manifest would remove the wait.

See the valley route

Keep the second scanner station through the winter peak, when volume doubles

The station is on loan until November.

See the numbers

Publish cut-off times

Customers who know the bulky freight cut-off book earlier, which spreads the evening load across two more hours.
